---
title: "Adapters"
description: "The uniform interface over statsforecast, mlforecast, neuralforecast and plain callables."
---

A `ForecasterAdapter` is the uniform interface a `ConformalMethod` talks to. It
converts library-specific objects — Nixtla long-format DataFrames, for instance —
into the numpy arrays a method's array surface consumes, so the calibration math
never sees framework types.

Four adapters ship with the package:

| Adapter | Wraps | Extra | Worked example |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CallableAdapter` | any function | none | [Exogenous features](../capabilities/exogenous) |
| `StatsForecastAdapter` | statsforecast | `nixtla` | [StatsForecast](statsforecast) |
| `MLForecastAdapter` | mlforecast | `nixtla` | [MLForecast](mlforecast) |
| `NeuralForecastAdapter` | neuralforecast | `nixtla` | [NeuralForecast](neuralforecast) |

## Capabilities

Optional features are mixins. An adapter inherits only the ones it implements, a
method declares what it needs through `REQUIRED_CAPABILITIES`, and the check runs
where the forecaster is bound — at the top of `calibrate` / `calibrate_cv`.

| | Refit | Quantiles | Bootstrap | CV | CV + quantiles |
|---|:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:|
| `CallableAdapter` | – | – | – | – | – |
| `StatsForecastAdapter` | ✅ | ✅ | – | ✅ | ✅ |
| `MLForecastAdapter` | ✅ | – | – | ✅ | – |
| `NeuralForecastAdapter` | ✅ | ✅ | – | ✅ | ✅ |

Two consequences worth knowing before you pick one:

- **`CallableAdapter` declares nothing**, so it works with `calibrate()` and
  explicit arrays but not `calibrate_cv()`. It is the simplest way to wrap a
  model you already have, and the workhorse of the test suite. A
  quantile-capable variant lives in `tests/helpers.py`.
- **`MLForecastAdapter` has no quantile support**, so it cannot back
  `ConformalizedQuantileRegression`. Calibration fails immediately rather than
  at predict time.

::: {.callout-important}
## Capability errors surface at calibration, never in `predict()`

```python
method = ConformalizedQuantileRegression(alpha=0.1)  # config only, always fine
# Raises UnsupportedCapability here, before any forecasting.
method.calibrate_cv(point_forecaster, n_windows=20)
```

This is a deliberate contract: a fitted object is only ever built after the
check passed, so the adapter it holds is known to support everything it will
need.
:::

### Capabilities that depend on configuration

`ForecasterAdapter.supports()` defaults to an `isinstance` check, but an adapter
may override it when a capability depends on runtime configuration rather than on
the class. `NeuralForecastAdapter` does exactly this: it inspects the model's
loss, so a point-loss model fails `ConformalizedQuantileRegression` calibration
while an `MQLoss` model of the same class succeeds. It also refuses the quantile
and refit capabilities when the model has exogenous features.
`StatsForecastAdapter` does the same when `exog_features` is set, and
`MLForecastAdapter`, which has no quantile path, refuses refit when `exog_features` is set.

## Lazy imports

`StatsForecastAdapter`, `MLForecastAdapter` and `NeuralForecastAdapter` are
re-exported lazily from `conformalforecast.adapters`, so importing the package
never pulls in statsforecast, mlforecast, neuralforecast or torch; the library is
only imported when you first touch the adapter that needs it. Without the extra
installed, that first access raises `ImportError` with the exact command:

```bash
pip install conformalforecast[nixtla]
```

`CallableAdapter` is always available; it is pure numpy.

## Writing your own

Inherit `ForecasterAdapter` plus the capability mixins you implement, and
implement every abstract method including the keyword-only `X=None` on
`predict`/`predict_batch`/`cross_validate` and the `aligned` CV mode. Read
`adapters/callable.py` first, it is the smallest complete example, and
[Exogenous features](../capabilities/exogenous) shows it wrapping a real model.
